A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VILA-U work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. v2 ends after its references; v3 includes Appendices A-C. All supplied material supports comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original VILA-U reconstruction, image/video understanding, image-generation and ablation results, alongside qualitative generation examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative video-generation results on VBench and qualitative results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The text-aligned vision tower, contrastive/reconstruction objectives, residual quantization, depth transformer and multimodal next-token training remain unchanged. The failed-training recipes move from Section 3.1 to Appendix C without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds VBench evaluation within the existing video-generation task. Appendix B also broadens qualitative in-context scenarios to arithmetic, art-style recognition and French-language descriptions. Training corpora and the existing understanding and image-generation benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: The comparison set expands across several capabilities. Table 2 adds Emu2-Chat, MM-Interleaved, DEEM and SEED-LLaMA; Table 3 adds Emu2-Chat and SEED-LLaMA. Table 4 adds SD v2.1, previously compared only on GenAI-Bench. New Table 6 compares video generation with Open-Sora, CogVideo and CogVideoX.

E3.justification: The added VBench evaluation introduces total, quality and semantic scores for video generation. Appendix B.3 also reports testing all in-context examples from VILA. No revision to the retained experiments' preprocessing, training-data quantities, VILA-U configurations or CFG settings is reported.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds qualitative reconstruction comparisons at 256/384 resolution and further understanding, in-context learning and generation case studies. The quantitative contrastive-loss and CFG ablations remain unchanged, matching v2 Tables 6-8 to v3 Tables 7-9. Appendix C relocates existing failed-recipe analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed specifications, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds quantitative video-generation findings where v2 supplied only examples. Table 6 reports VILA-U scores of 74.01 total, 76.26 quality and 65.04 semantic; its total exceeds CogVideo's 67.01 but trails Open-Sora's 75.91 and CogVideoX's 81.61. New comparator scores and Appendix B outputs further expand the evidence. Retained numerical results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1-7 retain the same combined objective, residual-quantization definitions and text/visual likelihood formulations. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contribution claims remain substantively unchanged: a single autoregressive framework unifies visual understanding and generation through text-aligned discrete visual features and high-quality training data. The added experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v3's conclusion replaces the explicit understanding/generation performance-gap limitations with discussion of balancing reconstruction against alignment and a new admission that significant mutual enhancement between understanding and generation has not been observed. Section 3.1 also softens 'cannot converge' to difficulty training from scratch.

D1.justification: The disclosed architecture, codebook size, residual depths, image resizing, dataset quantities and CFG setting remain unchanged. Project/code access information is retained. The new appendices do not supply substantive additional implementation details or detailed VBench execution settings.

R1.justification: The introduction and new Appendix A expand positioning around reconstruction-only VQGAN tokenizers versus quantized CLIP features, explicitly discussing SEED-LLaMA, AnyGPT and LaVIT. Section 2 removes the BLIP-style/LLaVA-style taxonomy and adds newer unified, autoregressive and video-generation literature. Tables 4-5 also relabel Show-o from discrete diffusion to autoregressive without explaining the change.

P1.justification: The introduction, related-work discussion and conclusion receive targeted rewrites, while failed-training discussion moves to Appendix C. Appendix organization, cross-references, author information and citation style change, but the six main sections and most technical prose remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds the VBench table and six qualitative figures covering reconstruction, understanding, in-context learning and generation. Existing comparison tables gain rows and several tables move. ICLR formatting changes the title, headers, typography and citation appearance; Figures 1-7 retain their content.

improvement.justification: The VBench comparison adds quantitative support for video-generation claims previously illustrated only qualitatively, while broader baselines and Appendix B strengthen the evidence. The explicit lack-of-synergy limitation improves qualification. These are useful but limited gains: the new evaluation is sparsely documented, explicit performance-gap caveats disappear from the conclusion, and Show-o's reclassification remains unexplained.
